name: Globster
description: An unidentified, often large, fibrous organic mass washed up on a shoreline. Once a staple of cryptozoological speculation, almost every well-studied globster has been identified by DNA or histology as the decomposed remains of a whale or other large vertebrate.
origin: Globsters have been reported on coastlines globally — Atlantic, Pacific, Indian Oceans, and adjacent seas. The phenomenon is not regional in any meaningful sense; it tracks the geography of large cetacean populations and shipping/observer density.
